title: Latency split, done right: the gyro is ~15 ms stale
question: With the robot standing, where does the 15-22 ms actually live — mechanics or sensing?
headline: Gyro response 16-31 ms (median ~19) vs encoder motion 18-23 ms: the two nearly coincide, so stiction/backlash takeup is only ~3 ms and the bundle is dominated by the SENSING pipeline — angular_velocity() is ~15 ms stale before our 30 ms filter. Total hardware dead time ~20 ms matches what the sim already models, so unmodeled lag is NOT the sim's fragility; static friction and stall_torque move to the top. And run 30's result deepens: the robot balances with ~105 ms of total rate-channel lag.
hub_output: part 3: stand the robot UP on the ground, steady it lightly. 6 trials.
part 3 done: gyro-response minus ~1 ms of body spin-up = sensing lag.
compare with part 2: encoder time - gyro time ~= stiction/backlash takeup
